title: Mucopolysaccharidosis type I (MPS I)
synonyms: عديد السكاريد المخاطي من النوع الأول
summary: MPS I happens when the body cannot break down large sugar molecules. They build up in many parts of the body, including the joints, heart, eyes and sometimes the brain.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the IDUA gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A child with two changed copies has MPS I. It ranges from severe to milder forms. Treatments exist and work best when started early, under a specialist team.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has MPS I. Could I be a carrier?
Can MPS I skip a generation?
What does a test for the IDUA gene involve?
card_summary: Large sugar molecules build up in many parts of the body. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Affects many parts of the body; treatments work best started early.
care: Specialist metabolic clinics, transplant and enzyme treatment centres, genetic counselling and family support groups.
